chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from Sahl ibn Zyad, who said: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Aqabah narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad (son of the sister of Abu Malik), from Abdullah ibn Sin'an, from Abd al-Wahid ibn al-Mukhtar, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about playing chess.
He (peace be upon him) replied: 'Indeed, the believer is occupied (from) play.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about playing chess?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) characterizes chess as a distraction that occupies the believer’s time, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *ghina* (self-sufficiency from trivialities) and mindfulness (*muraqaba*). This ruling is often interpreted not merely as prohibition but as a recommendation to prioritize spiritual and intellectual pursuits over leisure that may lead to negligence of duties.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-92 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with him- narrated that his father quoted on the authority of Sahl ibn Zyad, on the authority of Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Ja’far ibn Aqabah, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Ukht Abi Malik, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sin’an that Abolvahid ibn al-Mukhtar said, “I asked Aba Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) about playing chess.
He (MGB) replied, ‘A believer avoids playing it.’”
